texts.preamble: Mohd. Shahrukh vs . Sarukh & Ors. on 6 September, 2022 :1: In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 716/18 Fir no.: 118/18 Ps : Okhla Industrial Area U/s : 279/338 Ipc Mohd. Shahrukh Vs. Sarukh & Ors. Cnr No.:DLSE01-005496-2018 Mohd. Shahrukh S/o Ali Hasan R/o H. No.929/40, Zakir Nagar, Jamia Nagar, New Delhi. ......Claimant/Petitio Versus 1. Sarukh S/o Shamshad Khan R/o G-13/14, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi. ............Driver/Respondent 2. Salman S/o S/o Shamshad Khan R/o G-13/14, Sangam Vihar, New Delhi. ............Owner/Respondent no. 2 2. Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd. Golden Heights, Fourth Floor, No.1/2 59th C Cross, 4th M Block, Rajajinagar, Bangalore. .........Insurance Company/Respondent no. 2 Date of accident : 10.04.2018 Date of filing of Dar : 05.07.2018 Mact No. 716/18 Mohd. Shahrukh Vs. Sarukh & Ors. Page No. Date of Decision : 06.09.2022 Award Mohd. Shahrukh vs . Sarukh & Ors. on 6 September, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196209125/ 1 1.
texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 10.04.2018 at about 10.20 AM, petitioner / injured was riding on is motorcycle bearing no. DL 3SDR -1772 from Okhla towards Pul Prahaladpur through Ma Anandmai Marg. When he reached at Traffic Signal near Honda Show Room, offending vehicle in question bearing no. HR 55X 1019 driven by R-1 in a rash and negligent manner and a high speed came from ESI Hospital, Okhla Phase-1 side and hit the motorcycle of petitioner / injured. As such, due to such sudden and forceful impact, petitioner fell down along with motorcycle and received grievous injuries. Injured was removed to ESI hospital, Okhla Phase-1, New Delhi where his MLC bearing no. 136/18 dated 10.04.2018 was prepared. Further, he shifted to Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi on the same day and thereafter, he took treatment from Holy Family hospital. It is further stated that he remained bed ridden for about 9 months. He also received permanent disability. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 12.04.2022 noticing 33% permanent physical impairment in relation to right lower limb. 3. An FIR bearing No. 118/18 u/s 279,338 IPC PS Okhla Industrial Area, New Delhi was registered in this case. Page No. 2 of 23 4. Initially in response to DAR, respondent No.1/ driver and R-2/owner as well as insurance company appeared. Further as per record, no reply filed on behalf of driver and owner and they stopped appearing / participating in the present proceedings. 5. But reply/ legal offer filed by insurance company. In nutshell, in reply filed by insurance company in question, it is stated that the driving license of the driver in question was not valid to drive the commercial vehicle / taxi. It is further stated that the driver was not holding valid commercial license at the time of accident. Thus, it is stated that there is a violation of terms and condition of insurance policy. It is further stated that alleged offending vehicle was not possessessing a certificate of fitness. As such no legal offer was made by insurance company. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 20.09.2018 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 10.04.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR 55X 1019 being driven by R1, owned by R-2 and insured with R3? Whether the injured is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?OPP 3. Relief. 7. Petitioner filed his examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. He relied upon various documents Ex.PW1/1 to Ex.PW1/9. 8. Such PW-1/ Victim/ Injured / Petitioner was cross examined by Ld. MACT No. 716/18 Mohd. Shahrukh Vs. Sarukh & Ors. 9. It may be noted that driver and owner did not lead any evidence nor they cross examined the petitioner. Further, Ld. counsel for petitioner as well as respondent insurance company filed written arguments.
texts.arguments: 13. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. A person is not MACT No. 716/18 Mohd. Shahrukh Vs. Sarukh & Ors. Page No. 4 of 23 only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. It may be noted that in this background that in Cholamandlam Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD-Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet u/s 279/304 A IPC are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. This means that the Tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence: MACT No. 716/18 Mohd. Shahrukh Vs. Sarukh & Ors. Page No. 10 of 23 (i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary; (ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement; (iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb, then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,that is, the permanent disability suffered by the person. In the background of such fact proved on record by insurance company in this particular case and having regard to the ratio and direction by Hon'ble Supreme Court, three judges bench judgment of "National Insurance Company v. Swaran Singh ((2004) 3SCC 297)", the compensation will be payable in the first instance by the insurance company, but with liberty to recover the same from the driver-cum-owner of the offending vehicle in question. 46. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Even in the case of literate persons, the Tribunals are automatically ordering investment of MACT No. 716/18 Mohd. Shahrukh Vs. Sarukh & Ors. Page No. 19 of 23 the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit without recording that having regard to the age or fiscal background or the strata of the society to which the claimant belongs or such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks it necessary to direct such investment in the larger interests of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded to him.
